title: M/S Awadh Steels & Alloys (P) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunil Ambwani and Aditya Nath Mittal, JJ.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed as having become infructuous.
headnote: A challenge to Clause 4.55 of the U.P. Electricity Distribution Code, 2002 — bank-guarantee security only for contracted load exceeding 10 MW — became infructuous after that Code was repealed. Clause 4.20 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 makes security common for all heavy consumers and does not distinguish by load. Petition dismissed as infructuous.
facts: The petitioners, industrial consumers, challenged Clause 4.55 of the U.P. Electricity Distribution Code, 2002, as discriminatory: consumers with contracted load exceeding 10 MW could furnish security by bank guarantee, while other large and heavy industrial consumers below 10 MW could not. An interim order dated 27 March 2003 allowed them to submit a bank guarantee for the demanded security deposit. The 2002 Distribution Code was later repealed and replaced by the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.holding: Section 47 of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides for reasonable security to be determined by the Regulation.

After repeal of the U.P. Electricity Distribution Code, 2002, Clause 4.20 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 does not distinguish among heavy consumers by contracted load and makes security common for all such categories. The challenge to Clause 4.55 of the 2002 Code (bank-guarantee option only for load exceeding 10 MW) had therefore become infructuous, and the writ petition was dismissed as such.

not_decided.point: Whether Clause 4.55 of the 2002 Distribution Code unlawfully discriminated among large and heavy industrial consumers on contracted load for bank-guarantee security
not_decided.note: Not reached; petition dismissed as infructuous after repeal of the 2002 Code.
